steps.heading: merge() joins on a key
steps.body: df.merge(other, on='column') combines two DataFrames by matching rows where the join column has the same value, the same idea as a SQL JOIN.

steps.heading: Keep only what matches
steps.output:
#   region  ...  manager
# 0   West  ...    Priya
# 1   East  ...     Omar
steps.caption: how='inner' (the default) keeps only rows whose key exists on both sides.

steps.heading: how= controls what survives
steps.body: 'left' keeps every row from the left DataFrame even without a match (filling gaps with NaN); 'outer' keeps every row from both sides; 'inner' keeps only rows present in both.

steps.heading: Don't lose unmatched rows
steps.output: # North rows kept, with manager = NaN (no manager listed for North)
steps.caption: You'll practice inner/left/outer joins and simple concat() stacking in the cards that follow.
